query:
While Jerome was walking Cecilia through a PixInsight Ha-RGB blending workflow, someone in the chat acknowledged following the walkthrough closely but explicitly positioned themselves as outside the narrowband-PixInsight process. Who was that person?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Ruth
C. Marcus
D. Tomás
context:
[1] (about=Ruth, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:37:00) I cannot speak to the technical aspects but the image looks beautiful. Is it possible that what you have both done this evening is exactly the kind of collaboration that makes this group worth belonging to?
[2] (about=Dev, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:41:00) is that a dumb question but... if I wanted to learn PixInsight where would I even start? lowkey the walkthrough Jerome just did made more sense to me than any YouTube video I've tried
[3] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:32:00) Jerome I just ran the PixelMath blend on the Orion stack and I am SHAKING. The HII emission structure around the running man nebula that I have never been able to pull out is RIGHT THERE. I had completely written off narrowband blending as too technical for me and too cold-looking. This is totally different from what I imagined, the broadband colours are intact and the Ha just adds this incredible red-gold depth to the emission zones!!! I genuinely thought I hated narrowband because it looked monochromatic but you've just shown me I was wrong about the whole thing!!! 😍🌟📷
[4] (about=Harriet, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:39:00) I am going to put this whole thread in the podcast episode notes. The PixInsight walkthrough in a WhatsApp chat is a very particular kind of knowledge transfer that I think speaks to how amateur astronomy communities actually work. Jerome, you are better at teaching than you think you are.
[5] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:11:00) that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:42:00) Dev, I would recommend mastering the eyepiece before the software. In my experience learning to process an image before you understand what you are looking at produces technically sharp meaningless pictures. But the question is a good one and Jerome is the right person to answer it.
[7] (about=Priya, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:36:00) that Orion Ha-RGB is genuinely striking Cecilia. the HII emission around the running man is real ionised hydrogen, your image is now showing actual physics. that's the line between pretty picture and science image 🌟
[8] (about=Tomás, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:13:00) I'm reading this walkthrough and I have absolutely no idea what's happening technically but I can tell from the before and after results you two post that it works. Jerome you'd never do this kind of thing for my DSLR workflow though would you 😄🌌
agent_answer:
D. Tomás

Tomás said: "I'm reading this walkthrough and I have absolutely no idea what's happening technically... Jerome you'd never do this kind of thing for my DSLR workflow though would you 😄🌌" — he acknowledged following the walkthrough (reading it closely) while explicitly placing himself outside the narrowband-PixInsight technical process.
